transcript.text: My Hotpoint washer dryer isn't drying properly any more and there's a funny smell when it's on the dry bit. Is there something I should clean?

Yes, there are two very common things to clean on a Hotpoint washer-dryer that would explain both the poor drying and the smell. The 'funny smell' you hear during the dry phase is almost always lint or fluff scorching on the hot heating element because airflow is blocked. If the filter or condenser is clogged, heat builds up, smells burn, and the clothes stay damp. Before we look at any internal parts, please do these two owner-safe checks:
1. Unplug the machine for safety.
2. Check the lint filter (usually behind a small flap at the bottom front). If it is full of fluff, clean it thoroughly under running water and let it dry before replacing it.
3. Consider the load size: washer-dryers can only dry about half the amount they wash. If you put a full washing basket into the drying cycle, it will never dry properly and may smell because the drum is too packed for air to circulate. Please let me know if the filter was blocked and how large the load was (e.g., 'just 2 towels' or 'a full duvet').

I didn't know there was a filter to clean, so I haven't checked it. I usually dry a full wash load in one go, about 8-9kg. The smell is like burning dust or scorched fabric, and the top of the machine feels very hot. I thought I saw a faint haze near the door seal once too. I've still been using it, though.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. Please stop using the machine immediately. The combination of a 'burning dust' smell and the top of the cabinet feeling very hot indicates that fluff is scorching on the heating element because it cannot escape. This is an active fire hazard. Drying a full load traps heat and fluff, causing exactly this overheating and poor drying result. Because there has been significant overheating, I cannot advise you to simply clean it and carry on. 1. 2. 3. Please unplug the appliance now and arrange for an engineer to check it before using it again.

candidates: Restricted airflow (blocked lint filter/condenser) causing fluff scorching and poor drying (high)
Faulty drying heater or thermal cut-out (low)

claimsRejected.claim: The thermal cut-outs (safety devices) are intact and not damaged by heat.
The heating element itself hasn't melted or shorted.
There is no hidden damage to the internal wiring or insulation from the excessive heat.
You mentioned you usually dry a full 8-9kg load; washer-dryers typically have a maximum drying capacity of around 4-5kg (half the wash size).
The 'haze' you saw was likely lint being forced out through gaps because the internal airflow path is blocked.
